intro: Buying a home in Utah requires balancing your mortgage payment with property taxes, homeowners insurance and other recurring ownership expenses. Whether you're purchasing a family home near Salt Lake City, a townhouse in Provo or a property in St. George, understanding these costs can help you avoid borrowing more than your household can afford.

Our free Utah mortgage calculator estimates your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and repayment period. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable association fees to compare properties and establish a realistic purchase budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Utah?

blocks.markdown:
A $490,000 Utah home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $2,350.24.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. Property taxes, insurance premiums and the interest rate are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Utah housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/UT/HSG860224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $489,400 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $2,009, while the homeownership rate was 70.2%.

These historical figures include existing homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They do not represent current home sale prices.

Housing expenses along the Wasatch Front may differ considerably from those in southern Utah or smaller rural communities.

Buyers considering mountain properties should also investigate insurance availability, seasonal access and infrastructure maintenance.

Research recent comparable property sales within your preferred neighborhood before choosing a purchase price for the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Utah Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Choose your preferred mortgage repayment period and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees.

Add private mortgage insurance if required by your conventional financing.

Review your estimated monthly housing payment and adjust individual inputs to compare different borrowing arrangements.

The amortization schedule shows how much of each mortgage payment goes toward interest and reducing your outstanding balance.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing scenarios outside Utah.

sections.heading: How Utah Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Utah calculates residential property taxes using property valuations, applicable exemptions and local tax rates.

County assessors determine property values, while applicable taxing authorities establish the rates used to fund public services.

Understanding Utah's primary residential exemption is particularly important because it can substantially reduce the taxable value of an eligible property.

### Utah's 45% primary residential exemption

According to the [Utah State Tax Commission](https://tax.utah.gov/propertytax/locally-assessed/residential/), qualifying primary residential properties receive an exemption equal to 45% of their fair market value.

The remaining 55% represents the taxable property value.

The exemption generally applies to qualifying residential improvements and up to one acre of associated land per residential unit.

Properties occupied by qualifying long-term tenants may also receive this benefit. However, vacation homes and other nonqualifying residences generally remain taxable at their full fair market value.

### Utah property tax calculation example

Suppose your home's fair market value is $490,000 and the property qualifies for the primary residential exemption.

Assume a hypothetical combined local property tax rate of 1.10%.

Under the same hypothetical rate, a nonqualifying second home valued at $490,000 would have annual property taxes of $5,390.

This comparison demonstrates why property classification matters when estimating housing expenses.

Actual tax liabilities depend on local rates, property valuations and applicable adjustments.

sections.heading: Utah Residential Exemption Rules Starting in 2027

blocks.markdown:
The Utah State Tax Commission has published updated application requirements under legislation enacted in 2026.

Beginning January 1, 2027, changes in property ownership generally require the owner to submit Form TC-473A to establish or maintain eligibility for the primary residential exemption.

Additional application requirements apply when a property previously did not qualify or county officials have reason to question its eligibility.

A qualifying primary residence generally must serve as the occupant's principal domicile for at least 183 consecutive days during the calendar year.

The published application deadline is September 15. Missing the deadline may result in losing the exemption for the applicable tax year.

Review the [Utah primary residential exemption application guidance](https://tax.utah.gov/propertytax/tax-relief/primary-residential-exemption/) and confirm your obligations with the county before purchasing.

Do not assume the previous owner's exemption will automatically continue after an ownership transfer.

Insurance costs depend on your property's location, construction materials, replacement cost, condition and selected coverage.

Utah homeowners may experience wildfires, earthquakes, flooding, heavy snowfall and other weather-related damage.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Earthquake insurance along the Wasatch Front

Earthquake exposure deserves particular attention when purchasing properties near Salt Lake City, Ogden and other Wasatch Front communities.

The [Utah Insurance Department's disaster preparedness guide](https://insurance.utah.gov/consumers/disaster-preparedness/) explains that typical homeowners insurance policies exclude earthquake damage.

Separate policies or endorsements may provide additional protection.

For example, a hypothetical 10% earthquake deductible on $400,000 of dwelling coverage would represent $40,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered dwelling loss.

Review coverage limits and deductibles before selecting a policy.

### Wildfire and flood insurance

Properties near forests, grasslands and mountain communities may have additional wildfire insurance considerations.

Ask whether your property's location affects available coverage, premiums or required protective measures.

Standard homeowners insurance also generally excludes flooding and certain types of earth movement.

Investigate potential flood exposure through the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Include applicable additional insurance premiums when estimating your monthly housing payment.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly housing expenses rather than principal and interest alone.

Utah Housing Corporation provides mortgage financing and purchase assistance through approved participating lenders.

### Utah Housing FirstHome and HomeAgain loans

The [Utah Housing Corporation](https://utahhousingcorp.org/) offers mortgage programs designed for qualifying first-time and repeat buyers.

FirstHome primarily serves eligible first-time homebuyers, while HomeAgain provides financing opportunities for qualifying repeat buyers and other eligible households.

Credit, household income, property eligibility and purchase price requirements depend on the selected program.

Utah Housing also provides secondary mortgage financing to help qualifying borrowers cover down payments and closing expenses.

Confirm current assistance percentages, interest rates and repayment periods with a participating lender.

### Utah $20,000 First-Time Homebuyer Assistance Program

Under [Utah Code Section 63H-8-502](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title63H/Chapter8/63H-8-S502.html), qualifying first-time homebuyers may receive up to $20,000 toward purchasing an eligible newly constructed residence.

The assistance can be used toward the down payment, closing costs or a permanent mortgage interest rate reduction.

Published Utah Housing program guidelines identify a maximum purchase price of $450,000.

The assistance is structured as interest-free deferred financing rather than an unconditional grant.

Repayment obligations may arise when the property is sold or the mortgage is refinanced.

Funding is subject to legislative appropriations and availability. Confirm that funds remain available before relying on the program.

A shorter repayment period can substantially reduce lifetime interest expenses.

For a $392,000 mortgage at an illustrative 6% fixed interest rate, a 15-year repayment period would require approximately $3,307.91 monthly in principal and interest.

The equivalent 30-year mortgage would require approximately $2,350.24 monthly.

The shorter repayment period increases monthly expenses but reduces the number of years over which interest accrues.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Utah Home

blocks.markdown:
Utah homeowners should consider expenses beyond regular mortgage payments.

Water consumption, landscaping, summer cooling and winter heating can influence household budgets.

Properties in mountain communities may require snow removal, private road maintenance or additional insurance.

Condominium and townhouse buyers should review association budgets, reserve funds and potential special assessments.

Ask about existing maintenance obligations before making an offer.

Use our [Utah Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/utah-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax income and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing borrowing commitments.

Compare financing offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain sufficient emergency savings for closing expenses, insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $490,000 Utah home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $2,350.24 monthly. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### What is Utah's primary residential property tax exemption?

Qualifying primary residences receive a 45% exemption on eligible fair market value, leaving 55% subject to property taxation. Beginning January 1, 2027, updated application requirements apply following changes in ownership.

### Does Utah offer $20,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. Utah's First-Time Homebuyer Assistance Program authorizes up to $20,000 in assistance for qualifying buyers of eligible newly constructed homes. Funding availability, purchase price restrictions and repayment conditions apply.
